text:
marco: Quick canary update — ran a tiny hybrid late-fallback + speculative decode flow on dolly3-70b-8q4 (quantized) against baseline full-decode. Short summary: ~1.9x tokens/sec, ~18% token cost reduction, but small quality regressions on instruction tasks.

marco: Repro command I used: 
```bash
python run_decode_benchmark.py --model dolly3-70b-8q4 --speculative True --late_fallback=True --fallback_cutoff=0.12 --batch=8 --seq=1024 --eval-sets instruct-suite,mmlu --out out/canary1.json
```

cheng: Nice. Do you have per-dataset diffs? overall numbers are fine but we need to know where it regressed.

marco: Put the quick numbers in the output file. TLDR: instruct-suite accuracy -1.1% absolute (mostly step-by-step reasoning prompts), MMLU -0.7 points. LM perplexity unchanged on generic text.

lisa: Any pattern on length or temperature? Speculative decode often hurts longer reasoning sequences.

marco: Good call — the regressions cluster > 200 tokens and when temperature >= 0.7. At temp=0.2 it matches baseline more closely.

sam: Were you using KV cache warmup / prefix caching? That can interact badly with late fallback if cache misses happen.

marco: Yes default cache warmup enabled. I also tried disabling prefix cache (quick run) and the regression magnitude dropped ~0.3%.

eva: Did you compare top-k/top-p differences between spec path and fallback path? We sometimes see distribution shift when fallback triggers mid-token.

marco: We keep sampling policy identical, but the speculative path returns a short candidate then the fallback verifies with full logits. The mismatch appears when the verify step chooses a different token because of accumulated KV differences.

cheng: Can you attach the small example where it diverged? A 1-2 prompt pair would help.

marco: Copied one case below:
"""
Prompt: "Explain step-by-step how to reverse a linked list in-place."
Baseline (full): "1) initialize prev=null, cur=head ..."
Hybrid spec: "1) set prev=head.next ..."  <-- incorrect ordering, leads to wrong algorithmic step.
"""

lisa: Oof. That's a real correctness issue. Probable cause: speculative candidate took a high-prob token early that changed attention keys for later positions.

sam: For next run, try reducing fallback_cutoff (make fallback more aggressive) and enable a short re-score window (like 8 tokens) instead of whole sequence verification. See if performance still holds.

marco: Will do. Thought: maybe quantization + speculative path amplifies small logit shifts. Plan: 1) run with fallback_cutoff=0.07, 2) try verify_window=8, 3) run temp sweep {0.0,0.2,0.5}, 4) longer eval (10k prompts) on instruct-suite.

eva: Also add an AB test against a tiny set of production prompts (we have the 500-probe set in evalpool) to catch real regressions early.

ops-bot: deploy: canary flow updated — hybrid-spec decoding enabled for model dolly3-70b-8q4 at 5% traffic in eu-west for 30m. Monitor: latency, token-rate, instruction-accuracy.

marco: Thanks — starting the swept runs now. I'll post a follow-up with per-prompt diffs and a minimal failing prompt list. If the fail rate stays >0.5% on instruction-suite we should rollback.

cheng: If you need help with the re-score window patch I can pair. Also file a quick experiment note with config in the repo (so QA can reproduce).

marco: Yep — creating a short PR with the benchmark script + config. Will ping when done. :thumbsup:

lisa: One more ask — record model KV drift stats (cosine between cached keys across spec vs baseline) if possible. Might be revealing.

marco: Good idea, adding KV drift logging. Back in ~2h with numbers.
